articles.headline: Embiid has season-high 37 and Brown adds 31 as 76ers beat Nets 135-123 without LeBron James
articles.description: — Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points, Jaylen Brown matched his season best with 31 and the superstars provided the Philadelphia 76ers with more than enough in LeBron James' absence to beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123 on Monday night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points, Jaylen Brown matched his season best with 31 and the superstars provided the Philadelphia 76ers with more than enough in LeBron James' absence to beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123 on Monday night.


              Brown added 13 rebounds but wasn't in the game for the finish after a collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter opened a cut on his head. Brown returned to the game wearing a headband after being treated, but then left again a few minutes later.


              James sat out on the second half of the 76ers' back-to-back games and Philadelphia improved to 4-0 without him. Tyrese Maxey finished with 24 points and nine assists. 


              Embiid had 24 points by halftime of what appeared would be a blowout. The Nets made it a game in the fourth quarter before the center helped turn them back, scoring six straight Philadelphia points to extend a six-point lead back into double figures and then making a 3-pointer with 51 seconds remaining after Brooklyn had climbed back within four.


              Julius Randle scored 33 points and Michael Porter Jr. added 25 for the Nets, who fell to 3-10. Second-year guard Nolan Traore matched his career high with 23 points.


              Embiid sat out the victory Sunday over Indiana in which James passed Jason Kidd to move into No. 3 on the NBA's career assists list. The 76ers didn't officially list Embiid as available Monday until about half an hour before the game, but it was clear he was fine. He had 13 points in the first quarter as Philadelphia took a 33-26 lead. 


              The Sixers made their first three shots in the second, and when they finally missed, Dean Wade dunked the rebound while being fouled for a three-point play and a 46-28 lead. They made nine of their first 11 shots in the period — and scored on the rebound of that second miss as well. The lead reached 63-39 on Maxey's 3-pointer before Philadelphia took a 78-59 lead to halftime. 


              The Nets charged back into the game in the third, cutting it to 105-95 headed to the fourth. Randle's 3-pointer trimmed it to 106-101 early in the period. 


              Up next
              76ers: Visit Orlando on Wednesday.


              Nets: Host Chicago on Wednesday.


              ------

articles.headline: Bane scores 24, Magic rally in 4th quarter to beat Celtics 115-105, extend win streak to 4 games
articles.description: — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night.
articles.body:
BOSTON -- — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night. 


              Franz Wagner, who entered the night having scored 30 or more points in each of Orlando’s previous four games, had 21 points, nine assists and eight rebounds. Anthony Black finished with 20 points and seven assists.


              The Magic shot 50% (41 of 82) from the field in the game to earn their first win in Boston since Dec. 18, 2022.


              It was Boston's first home loss of the season and snapped the team's six-game win streak. Jayson Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and 12 rebounds, his first double-double since their season-opening loss at Detroit. But he also had five of his team’s 11 turnovers. 


              Paul George added 22 points and Payton Pritchard had 21 points.


              The Magic, despite playing on three days of rest, struggled with their shot early. But they still managed to cobble together a 50-41 lead at halftime.


              Playing on the second night of a back-to-back, the Celtics showed some early signs of fatigue. But they found some traction in the third quarter, led by Tatum’s 14 points to outscore Orlando 36-25 in the period and take a 77-75 lead into the fourth.


              But the Magic recovered and got an alley-oop from Wagner to Wendell Carter Jr., followed by a jumper by Bane to take a 110-99 edge with 1:33 left.


              A night after finishing the first quarter with a franchise-high 33-point lead in its blowout win over Dallas, Boston needed a 3-pointer at the buzzer by Pritchard to even make it to 17 points by the end of the first period on Monday.


              Both teams had trouble scoring in the opening quarter. The Magic went 7 of 21 (33.3%) from the field, while the Celtics made only 6 of 24 (25%) shots. 


              Up next
              Magic: Host Philadelphia on Wednesday night.


              Celtics: Visit Denver on Wednesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Heat star Bam Adebayo exits win over Rockets early with hip tightness
articles.description: Heat star Bam Adebayo was ruled out of Monday's win over the Rockets after 16 first-half minutes due to hip tightness.
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Heat star big man Bam Adebayo left Monday's 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets with hip tightness and did not return.

Adebayo played 16 minutes in the first half and subbed out with 33 seconds left in the second quarter. He did not start the second half and was not seen on the Heat bench for the rest of the game.

Andrew Wiggins replaced Adebayo in the starting lineup on Monday. Miami's depth came alive Monday night with seven players scoring in double figures.

Giannis Antetokounmpo praised Adebayo as "one of the most versatile bigs I've ever played with" as his partner put up 37 points and 14 rebounds in Friday's win over Cavs.

Adebayo is the anchor of the Heat's defense and entered Monday's game averaging 19.5 points, 8.5 rebounds and a career-high 2.1 steals per game.

The 8-6 Heat have surged over the past two weeks, winning five straight games behind the duo of Antetokounmpo and Adebayo.

articles.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 20, Heat roll past Rockets 128-110 for 5th straight win
articles.description: — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17 and the Miami Heat never trailed on the way to beating the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday night for their fifth straight victory.
articles.body:
MIAMI -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17 and the Miami Heat never trailed on the way to beating the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday night for their fifth straight victory.


              Davion Mitchell had a 16-point, 10-assist night and Bobby Portis Jr. scored 16 points for the Heat, who have gone 8-2 since starting the season 0-4. Miami was without Bam Adebayo for the second half because of right hip tightness.


              Thompson made five 3-pointers for the Heat, giving him 2,952 for his career and moving him within 21 of Ray Allen (2,973) for third on the all-time 3s list. Antetokounmpo added six assists — and will now face his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks, for the first time on Wednesday.


              Alperen Sengun scored 23 points for the Rockets, who were on the second night of a back-to-back and saw their four-game winning streak end.


              Kevin Durant scored 22 for Houston; he's now up to 32,917 points in his career, 83 shy of the 33,000-point milestone. Only four players — LeBron James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant — have scored that many.


              Houston scored a season-high 147 points against Washington on Sunday night. Things went a little differently on Monday.


              The Rockets started 1 for 9 from the field and scored only two points in the first 5:54 against the Heat, setting the tone for a night where Houston played uphill the whole way. It was Houston's first loss in six games against Eastern Conference teams this season.


              The top eight teams in the Western Conference, entering Monday, were 22-3 against teams from the East — winning by an average of 13.4 points. None of those teams had lost to an East opponent by more than 11, before Monday.


              Up next
              Rockets: Visit Indiana on Wednesday night.


              Heat: Host Milwaukee on Wednesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Mike McCarthy on Steelers' blowout loss: 'Needs to stop there'
articles.description: After a deflating loss at Cincinnati, Pittsburgh faces a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- In the wake of a 20-point loss Sunday night, Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen was soft-spoken and introspective as he outlined two paths forward for his team.

"I think, for the most part, all of us are looking at ourselves and just knowing where we could have been better, what we could have done just to stop the bleeding here and there," he said. "The other way you could look at it is [that] it goes downhill, and we can just keep going downhill the whole season."

Monday afternoon, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy emphatically chose the former.

"This needs to be one game, and it needs to stop there," McCarthy said. "... This is a part of the journey of the season, but it needs to be one game, and that'll be our approach as we prepare for Philadelphia."

After a deflating 38-18 Week 10 loss, the Steelers face a Week 11 gut-check game at the Eagles on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

But just because McCarthy needs the loss to be a one-game speed bump in the Steelers' season doesn't mean it will be -- especially facing a cross-state rival in a city where the Steelers haven't won a regular-season game since 1965.

And though the Steelers had a history of resilience under former coach Mike Tomlin and posted a 12-2 record in games following a loss of 20 or more points, McCarthy's units haven't rebounded as successfully. McCarthy is 8-15 in games following a loss of at least 20 points, including a 2-8 record in Dallas. Even so, McCarthy dismissed the idea Sunday night that the loss could turn the tide of the season.

"Oh, wow," he said, somewhat incredulous at the question. "It's one loss, and it will be dealt with as much. I'm more focused on the details of the fundamentals and the things we needed to do.

"We're not going to drive down the drama road of those types of things. It's a waste of time. It's a waste of energy, and we're going to pour our energy into ourselves looking in the mirror and stay focused on the things that we can control."

The Steelers did that after each of their previous losses and responded with wins, including a four-game streak after the Thursday night loss in Cleveland during Week 4.

But Sunday night's loss at Cincinnati felt different. A win against one of the league's hottest teams could have legitimized Pittsburgh's 6-2 start to a national audience, solidified its standing as a serious postseason contender and validated a series of front office decisions, including bringing back quarterback Aaron Rodgers this offseason and also standing pat at this month's NFL trade deadline.

Though they entered Cincinnati as underdogs, the Steelers had reason to believe they could prove the sportsbooks wrong. Teams coming off a bye were undefeated in games against opponents who played in an international game the previous week. McCarthy was 12-6 after bye weeks. articles.headline: Mitchell and Allen power the Cavaliers to a 126-115 win over the Bulls
articles.description: — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night.


              Cleveland trailed by six points, 31-25, after one period before rebounding in the second. The Cavaliers used a 32-17 scoring edge in the second quarter for a 57-48 advantage at the break. Cleveland maintained its nine-point lead through the third quarter and weathered a fourth quarter comeback try by the Bulls to win for the third time in four games.


              Tyrese Proctor scored 10 of his 17 points in the first half for Cleveland, which improved to 6-2 at home. Peyton Watson chipped in 14 points, Meleek Thomas added 10 and James Harden finished with nine points and 10 assists.


              Norman Powell led Chicago with 27 points, and Matas Buzelis scored 23. Jalen Smith posted 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Tre Jones finished with 16 points and Isaac Okoro had 13.


              The loss halted the Bulls' two-game win streak, which followed an eight-game skid. Chicago fell to 2-6 on the road and 3-10 overall.


              The Cavaliers were without Evan Mobley, who has a sprained big toe on his right foot. Cleveland says he will be re-evaluated in seven to 10 days.


              Up next
              Bulls: At the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.


              Cavaliers: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Rams center Coleman Shelton out 4-6 weeks with hamstring injury
articles.description: Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Cardinals.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams center Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring and is expected to sit out the next four to six weeks, a team spokesperson said Monday.

Shelton sustained the injury in the second quarter of the Rams' Week 10 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. He had not missed an offensive snap this season for the Rams before his injury.

Shelton was replaced at center by Dylan McMahon, who played only nine offensive snaps before he injured his knee. The Rams said Monday that McMahon partially tore his patellar tendon and will be put on injured reserve.

Offensive lineman Beaux Limmer moved to center after McMahon's injury, and backup offensive lineman Bill Murray moved to left guard, playing 49 offensive snaps.

The injuries are just the latest for a Rams offense that is also currently without wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, tight end Terrance Ferguson, and guard Steve Avila.

The Rams, 6-4 after winning four games in a row, are on their bye this week. They host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12.

articles.headline: Sources: Jets QB Geno Smith avoided major ankle injury, testing shows
articles.description: Imaging tests performed on Jets quarterback Geno Smith's injured left ankle did not reveal any major concerns, sources said Monday.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith, who underwent imaging tests Monday on his left ankle, avoided a major injury, sources told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Smith dealt with a variety of injuries during Sunday's game, but his ankle provided the biggest concern. He will continue to be evaluated throughout the week, but the hope is that he will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

"He's good," a source told ESPN. "He'll be fine."

Coach Aaron Glenn declined to comment on the injury earlier Monday but emphasized that Smith remains New York's starter and pushed back on the notion of playing rookie Cade Klubnik for evaluation purposes.

"Geno's our starter," Glenn said on a videoconference with reporters. "Come on now, let's not do that.

"I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."

Smith exited twice in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He missed the first series of the third quarter due to a concussion evaluation, then returned for one series before hurting his ankle later in the quarter while falling backward on a knockdown by blitzing safety Cole Bishop.

The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.

The 36-year-old Smith, whose contract expires at the end of the season, is having a solid year as the Jets' bridge quarterback. He's 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions, but the Jets are only 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game).

Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.

The Jets' third quarterback is former Tennessee Titans second-round pick Will Levis, who is on the practice squad.

articles.headline: Kyle Hamilton rocks Christmas sweater ahead of 'MNF,' leads NFL Week 10 arrivals
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
Players across the NFL might want to look at the forecast before checking the mirror to finalize their Week 10 looks.

Sunday's arrivals offer plenty of opportunities to layer up. Morning temperatures in the 30s in Green Bay and the 40s in Cleveland could make wool coats, chunky knits and beanies practical additions to the pregame rotation. The chill extends south, too: Atlanta and Nashville are forecast to start Sunday near freezing before warming into the 50s.

Out West, sunglasses could be the accessory of choice. Mostly sunny skies and afternoon temperatures in the 70s in Glendale, Arizona, and upper 60s in Las Vegas favor lighter layers. Arlington, Texas, offers a different picture, with rain and temperatures hovering in the upper 40s -- another reason to give weather-ready outerwear a starring role.

Here are the standout looks from Week 10.

Monday night drip

It's never too early to get into the holiday spirit. Just look at Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton. He arrived for "Monday Night Football" in a Christmas sweater tied to Toyotathon that included reindeers flying with a car in front of them and the moon in the background.

Sunday's best

Ja'Marr Chase fashionably mixed business with comfort ahead of a high-stakes night. The Bengals receiver paired a glossy beige jacket and matching snap-button pants with a white shirt and dark tie, carrying his cleats into Cincinnati's primetime showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers with the AFC North lead on the line. 
Fernando Mendoza kept his first-start look simple. Ahead of his debut as the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback, he arrived in a navy bomber jacket with a dark shirt and pants, adding white sneakers and a smile to complete the look. 
Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young paired a blue-and-white striped Kith polo over a white long-sleeve shirt with light-wash jeans and coordinating sneakers. Clear-frame glasses and a Louis Vuitton suitcase rounded out his look.

Thursday night's fashion

Cam Skattebo brought plenty of flair to his arrival, sporting a custom Giants-themed Iron Man mask. He paired the silver-and-blue headgear with a black sweatshirt, khaki pants and layered chains.

articles.headline: Behind Raiders fans' tribute to Fernando Mendoza's mother
articles.description: Tom Joanides' social media campaign became a meaningful tribute when Mendoza scored in his first NFL start.
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders fan Tom Joanides, 46, had his first viral moment on social media for a good cause.

He went on X asking Raiders fans, who were attending Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium, to stay seated after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza scored his first touchdown.

The idea was meant to honor Mendoza's mother, Elsa, who has been confined to a wheelchair due to her multiple sclerosis diagnosis.

Watching the game at home with his family, Joanides saw thousands of Raiders fans remain in their seats while celebrating Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run in the first quarter of his first career start. Elsa and Mendoza's father, Fernando Mendoza Sr., were seated in a suite, cheering on their son.  "The fan base has an understanding that these are people; I'm shocked and elated that it actually happened. I've never had anything go viral ever," Joanides told ESPN. "But I'm not surprised that Raider Nation has the heart that it does."

Despite the Raiders losing to the Seahawks 21-13, Mendoza was "super grateful" for the fans' gesture, and it meant a lot to his family.

"On a dark day, that brings a smile to my face," Mendoza said postgame. 

In July, Joanides, a Los Angeles native, went on X and wrote a post, asking fans to stay seated whenever Mendoza scored his first touchdown at home.

However, his post didn't receive much traction.

"I don't have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void," Joanides said.

Five days before the Raiders' home matchup, Joanides went on X to reshare his message from the summer.

This time, the fan base heard him. Joanides' post received more than 800,000 views and close to 400 reposts.

Joanides, who began attending Raiders games with his dad when he was 3, said he would list "Raider Nation" as his ethnicity on government forms if he could.

Joanides was inspired after watching a Front Office Sports interview, in which Mendoza said he donated $500,000 to the University of Miami Health System and the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine to help fight against multiple sclerosis.

Mendoza's advocacy for the cause is inspired by Elsa, who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2008. His family launched the Mendoza Family Fund in April, which directly supports the National MS Society.

Through their foundation, Mendoza's family has raised more than $1 million.

"I just found it really touching," Joanides said. "This [was] an opportunity for this fan base to welcome [Mendoza] and his family in a very particular way and show what Raider Nation is all about."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's McKennie amid Pochettino arrival
articles.description: Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie, while Atlético Madrid are exploring a deal for Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested in United States men's national team midfielder Weston McKennie, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport. Incoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino admires the 28-year-old's versatility after working with him with the USMNT and could seek a reunion at Old Trafford. However, McKennie's club, Juventus, see him as central to head coach Luciano Spalletti's plans and are reluctant to sanction a January departure. His contract runs until June 2030.

- Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently among Manchester United's January targets under Pochettino, according to The Telegraph. The incoming head coach wants to strengthen his backline, with Bassey's pace and ability to cover at full back making him an attractive option. The Nigeria international's contract runs until next summer, although Fulham hold an option to extend it by a further 12 months.

- Chelsea continue to track Kerim Alajbegović, having come close to signing him before his summer move to Juventus, La Gazzetta dello Sport has revealed. The Serie A giants are determined to resist any efforts to lure him away from Turin. Alajbegović, 19, is contracted until 2031 and remains -- much like McKennie -- a key member of Spalletti's Juve squad. At this stage, no formal negotiations have taken place between the two clubs.

- Atlético Madrid are exploring a January move for Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, as per TEAMtalk. Diego Simeone's side are attracted by the prospect of pairing the 28-year-old with his Argentine teammate Cristian Romero, although Barcelona are also interested. Martínez has indicated he wants to leave United in 2027 and favours a move to Spain, with the Premier League club open to his departure as they look to reshape their squad.

- Brighton & Hove Albion, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are pursuing Juventus midfielder Adin Licina ahead of January, Tuttosport reports. The teenager is on loan at Cremonese, and Juventus remain reluctant to let him leave permanently before assessing his potential at Serie A level. Bayern Munich retain a preferential right and a 30% share of any future transfer fee.

articles.headline: Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt
articles.description: Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt.
articles.body:
Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe this season, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into the Argentina No. 10 shirt worn by the legendary Lionel Messi.

Paz is the son of Pablo Paz, who played for Argentina at the 1998 World Cup, and was born in Tenerife, Spain. He began his senior career at Real Madrid and spent three years with their B team, RM Castilla, but struggled to break into the first team. He made his debut in January 2022 -- and his international debut came a few months later -- yet only managed eight first-team appearances in all competitions before leaving for Como in August 2024 for around €6 million, though his contract included various clauses allowing Madrid to re-sign him.

Under former Barcelona, Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, himself in his first senior coaching job at Como, Paz developed incredibly. "He taught me practically everything," Paz told UEFA earlier this year. "I arrived here as a young player from Castilla. I'd played a few games for Real Madrid, but in the end I was a reserve-team player in a lower division.

"Coming here and playing in Serie A, the top flight, allowed me to grow and improve a lot, both as a player and as a person. It was all thanks to Cesc, who believed in me and brought me here. From the first day he let me play the way I wanted and gave me a lot of freedom. He taught me a lot. I think the player I am today is all down to him."

His form for Como took off and he has scored 25 goals and made 25 assists in his 89 games so far -- six goals and eight assists from 14 games this season. Obviously that saw plenty of transfer links, including to Arsenal and Chelsea, but a complicated deal saw Madrid agree to let Como take on his full rights for around €60 million this summer, with a clause for them to re-sign the player for €80 million in 2027 if they wish.

So who is Argentina's heir to Messi, now that the great man has retired from international football? And what do we need to know about his style of play? Sam Tighe and Tor-Kristian Karlsen explore.

Can Nico Paz replace Lionel Messi for Argentina?

Comparing anyone to arguably the greatest player the world has ever seen can feel cruel, but it's a rite of passage any young creative Argentine player must undertake -- particularly in the wake of Messi's international retirement and the fact that Paz will take over his No. 10 shirt.

In the seasons they turned 21 (and played a full campaign), Messi racked up 34 league goals contributions for Barcelona in 2008-09 -- the season that saw Barcelona win the Champions League and Messi score in the 2-0 win in the final. That split into 23 goals and 11 assists, and he overperformed his expected goals tally (11.85) by a huge margin.

Meanwhile, Paz was nowhere near those kinds of stats at age 21, as Como were still a rising force, vying for Champions League qualification (let alone playing in it), but he was at the heart of that charge, registering 18 l
